prose_updates.tldr: At the critical rare-arm boundary, the finite-population AIPW error need not be Gaussian. On this note's structured binary profile subclass, a stopped adaptive-to-Bernoulli-to-Poisson transfer and directed-rational convolution still give a computable atom-safe confidence interval with uniform randomization coverage and explicit oracle slack. Separately, capped clipped-ramp witnesses optimize the all-confidence-set late-void converse allowed by the outcome bound \(M\) and residual Lipschitz modulus \(L_r\): at diameter \(0<d<d_{\max}\), honesty forces limiting large-diameter probability at least \([(1-x(d))^c-2\alpha]_+\). The elbow \(d=M^2/L_r\) is interior exactly when \(L_r>M\), and exact attainment is confined to the selected two-sign subexperiment. Subclass inclusion transfers only the converse to Li and Zhao's baseline adaptive class. The exact \(1/8\), \(0.60710678\) ramp result and the high-hazard \(0.442M\) radius remain valid special results.

project_justification.gap: Li and Zhao's baseline adaptive-design class permits positive history-dependent assignment probabilities, but their Gaussian AIPW theorem requires a negligible-maximum condition that fails at bounded cumulative hazard. Existing adaptive and i.i.d. width results neither calibrate the signed atomic compound-Poisson law nor optimize the complete-log common-void obstruction under simultaneous \(M\)-boundedness and \(L_r\)-Lipschitz constraints.
project_justification.niche: The boundary has two distinct deliverables. Structured deterministic profiles permit computable atom-safe positive calibration. For all-estimator information limits, a capped clipped ramp saturates the pointwise envelope \(\min\{L_r(u-a)_+,M\}\), producing a quadratic-to-linear separation curve and the optimized late-void probability--diameter envelope.
project_justification.fill: The project supplies the finite adaptive-to-Poisson transfer and profile-net interval theorem on the declared structured subclass, plus an exact finite-sample clipped-ramp tradeoff and its optimized asymptotic envelope. A sourced subclass-inclusion argument lifts only that converse to Li and Zhao's larger baseline binary adaptive class. Pairwise attainment, positive calibration, the exact ramp certificate, and the high-hazard radius retain their separately stated scopes.

prose_updates.related_work: Li and Zhao (2026) provide the closest design-based setup: fixed finite-population potential outcomes, positive assignment probabilities that may be prespecified functions of history, and predictable AIPW regression. Their baseline binary class contains both the linear and capped clipped ramps, but their Theorem 4(ii) assumes Condition 3; these bounded-hazard witnesses fail its negligible-maximum part because late standardized increments remain nonnegligible. The present optimized converse therefore transfers by subclass inclusion, while its matching confidence-set construction remains sharp only inside each selected two-sign clipped-ramp experiment and the positive profile-net theorem remains confined to this note's structured subclass. Bibaut and Kallus (2025) organize adaptive inference into Gaussian repair, always-valid methods, and direct inversion of nonnormal laws. Waudby-Smith et al. (2024) provide predictable-logging confidence sequences, Freidling, Zhao, and Gao (2026) study selection-conditioned randomization tests, and Cho, Bibaut, and Kallus (2025) invert simulated adaptive laws; none supplies this finite-population signed atomic calibration or optimized common-void envelope. Chen et al. (2026) obtain a compound-Poisson HT law under independent Poisson importance sampling, while Hong, Leung, and Li (2020) treat limited overlap with diverging effective information. Shekhar and Ramdas (2023) prove i.i.d. bounded-mean width bounds rather than the present exact sequential two-sign tradeoff. Barbour and Xia (1999) support compound-Poisson error accounting, and Bhattacharjee and Goldstein (2019) identify the generalized Dickman constant-profile reduction. Liberali et al. (2025) remain the applied consumer, conditional on a prespecified expected-endpoint bridge for GUSTO-1 and EUROPA.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The finite-transfer theorem couples the AIPW statistic, not the complete experiments, and therefore does not imply the all-estimator lower bound. The optimized frontier instead uses the exact common subprobability on a late-arm void event. The clipped profile is optimal only within the declared late-void two-sign witness geometry under the existing \(M,L_r\) constraints; the matching procedure knows the selected pair, so it establishes no global minimax attainment over the full structured class. Subclass inclusion transfers the converse, but neither attainment nor positive calibration, to Li and Zhao's baseline class. The positive theorem still requires fixed profiles, deterministic domination for same-log threshold selection, and supplied profile and early-variation contracts. The \(0.442M\) high-hazard result remains a subfamily upper bound. The polynomial bit-complexity question remains open because no polynomial bound controls profile boxes that straddle the certification boundary.
prose_updates.honest_scope: Uniform finite-experiment coverage applies to the declared bounded Lipschitz intensity and signed-residual profile subclass with its supplied common profile event, early quadratic-variation envelope, and certified inputs. The all-confidence-set envelope \([(1-x(d))^c-2\alpha]_+\) is optimized among late-void two-sign witnesses under the existing \(M,L_r\) constraints. Exact attainment is only for the selected two-sign clipped-ramp subexperiment; no global minimax attainment is claimed for the structured class or Li and Zhao's larger baseline class. Only the converse transfers to that baseline class by subclass inclusion. The original linear-ramp frontier, the exact \(1/8\) and \(0.60710678\) specialization, the directed \(13/32\) certificate, and the high-hazard \(0.442M\) radius remain valid special results. No polynomial certificate-complexity exponent is asserted. The Liberali et al. application is conditional on a prespecified expected-endpoint bridge; random-profile, Cox-process, and atom-free quantile extensions remain outside scope.
